how adverb

also how?, in what way, the way that

classical

Vulg. Mt. 6.28: Cōnsīderāte līlia agrī quōmodo crēscunt
Sen. Ep. 77.20: quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta
Traupman 330

quōmodo (quō modō)

adverb, interrogative and relative

how? in what way?; as

Often written as two words (Catull. 10.7). As a relative it answers sīc: quōmodo … sīc, as … so.

Other words

  • quemadmodum — how; in the way that, as

    adverb, interrogative and relative · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: quaeris, quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam; Sen. Ep. 47.11: sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere

    Mostly in indirect questions and in comparisons.

  • quī — how? how ever?

    adverb (an old ablative of quī, quis) · also used · classical · Ter. And. 302: Quī scīs?; Phaedr. 1.1.7: quī possum, quaesō, facere quod quereris, lupe?

    Above all in short questions of speech: quī scīs?, how do you know?; quī potest?, how can it be? (Lewis & Short).

  • ut — how (of health and state)

    adverb, interrogative and exclamatory · also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 48–49: ut valēs, Megarōnidēs?; Traupman 330

    Ut valēs?, how are you? (see “how are you?”).

  • quam — how (to what degree)

    adverb, with adjectives and adverbs · also used · classical · Traupman 330

    Quam longē?, how far?; quam mox?, how soon?

Examples

  • Cōnsīderāte līlia agrī quōmodo crēscunt: nōn labōrant, neque nent.

    Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.Vulg. Mt. 6.28

  • quī possum, quaesō, facere quod quereris, lupe?

    how can I do what you complain of, wolf?Phaedr. 1.1.7

  • quaeris, quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam

    you ask how I lay out my day in summer at my Tuscan placePlin. Ep. 9.36.1

  • quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert

    as with a play, so with life: what matters is not how long but how well it has been actedSen. Ep. 77.20

  • quid esset jam Bīthȳnia, quō modō sē habēret

    what Bithynia was like now, how it was getting onCatull. 10.6–7

  • Salvē, anime mī. — Ō mī exspectāte, salvē. — Ut valēs? — Salvum advēnisse gaudeō.

    Hello, my darling. — Oh, how I’ve waited for you, hello. — How are you? — I’m glad you’re home safe.Ter. Haut. 406–407

See also how are you?, how much, how many, what kind of.
